authoredSolutions.1: The amplitude of the electric field is \(E_0=20\text{ NC}^{-1}\). The average energy density of an electromagnetic wave is \[u=\tfrac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0E_0^2.\] Energy contained in a volume \(V\) is \[U=uV=\tfrac{1}{2}\times 8.85\times10^{-12}\times(20)^2\times 5\times10^{-4}.\] \[U=\tfrac{1}{2}\times 8.85\times10^{-12}\times 400\times 5\times10^{-4}=8.85\times10^{-13}\text{ J}.\] Hence the correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.2: Reading the graph: \(0\) to \(5\text{ s}\) the velocity rises \(0\to 10\), area \(=\tfrac12(5)(10)=25\text{ m}\); \(5\) to \(10\text{ s}\) constant \(10\), area \(=50\text{ m}\); \(10\) to \(15\text{ s}\) rises \(10\to 20\), area \(=\tfrac12(10+20)(5)=75\text{ m}\); \(15\) to \(20\text{ s}\) falls \(20\to 0\), area \(=\tfrac12(5)(20)=50\text{ m}\). Total positive area \(=200\text{ m}\). From \(20\) to \(25\text{ s}\) the velocity is negative, reaching \(-20\), so the area is \(-50\text{ m}\). \[\text{distance}=200+50=250\text{ m},\qquad \text{displacement}=200-50=150\text{ m}.\] \[\frac{250}{150}=\frac{5}{3}.\] Hence the correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.3: For a uniform sphere \(M=\tfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3\rho\), so \[g=\frac{GM}{R^2}=\frac{4}{3}\pi G\rho R\propto \rho R.\] Therefore \[\frac{g_A}{g_B}=\frac{\rho\cdot R}{(\rho/3)\cdot 4R}=\frac{3}{4}.\] Hence the correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.4: At the point of slipping the limiting friction supplies the centripetal force: \[\mu mg=m\omega^2 r\ \Rightarrow\ r=\frac{\mu g}{\omega^2},\] so \(r\propto 1/\omega^2\). Halving \(\omega\) multiplies \(r\) by \(4\), giving \(r=4\times 1\text{ cm}=4\text{ cm}\). Hence the correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.5: In the figure each input is fed to a NOR gate with both of its inputs tied together, which acts as an inverter, giving \(\bar a\) and \(\bar b\). These feed a third NOR gate: \[Y=\overline{\bar a+\bar b}=a\cdot b,\] using De Morgan's theorem. The output is high only when both inputs are high, so the circuit is equivalent to an AND gate. Hence the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.6: Initially \(Q=CV\) and \(E_1=\tfrac12CV^2\). When the charged capacitor is connected in parallel to an identical uncharged one, the charge \(Q\) is shared and the common potential becomes \(V'=Q/(2C)=V/2\). The energy of the combination is \[E_2=\tfrac12(2C)\left(\frac{V}{2}\right)^2=\tfrac14CV^2=\frac{E_1}{2}.\] So \(E_2:E_1=1:2\) and the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.7: Let each filament have resistance \(R\). In parallel the combination is \(R/2\), in series it is \(2R\). At the same applied voltage and for the same time, \[H=\frac{V^2t}{R_{eq}}\ \Rightarrow\ \frac{H_p}{H_s}=\frac{R_{series}}{R_{parallel}}=\frac{2R}{R/2}=4.\] Hence the ratio is \(4:1\) and the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.8: For a transmitting antenna at ground level, the line-of-sight range to a receiving antenna of height \(h\) is \(d=\sqrt{2hR}\). Therefore \[h=\frac{d^2}{2R}=\frac{(4\text{ km})^2}{2(6400\text{ km})}=\frac{16}{12800}\text{ km}=1.25\times10^{-3}\text{ km}=1.25\text{ m}.\] Writing this as \(x\times10^{-2}\text{ m}\) gives \(x=125\). Hence the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.9: Capacitive reactance \(X_C=\dfrac{1}{2\pi fC}\propto \dfrac{1}{f}\), a rectangular-hyperbola shaped curve falling with frequency. Inductive reactance \(X_L=2\pi fL\propto f\), a straight line through the origin. In the graph curve \(A\) falls with \(f\) and curve \(B\) is a straight line rising through the origin, so \(A=X_C\) and \(B=X_L\). Hence the correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.10: Heat supplied \(\Delta Q=mL_v=1\times 2257=2257\text{ kJ}\). Work done against the constant atmospheric pressure is \[\Delta W=P\Delta V=1\times10^{5}\times(1.671-1.00\times10^{-3})=1.67\times10^{5}\text{ J}=167\text{ kJ}.\] By the first law, \[\Delta U=\Delta Q-\Delta W=2257-167=2090\text{ kJ}.\] Hence the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.11: For a denser-to-rarer interface, \(\sin i_C=\dfrac{1}{\mu}=\dfrac{v_{denser}}{v_{rarer}}\). With \(i_C=45^{\circ}\), \[v_{denser}=v_{rarer}\sin 45^{\circ}=\frac{3\times10^{8}}{\sqrt2}=2.12\times10^{8}\text{ m/s}.\] Hence the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.12: Einstein's equation gives \[eV_0=\frac{hc}{\lambda}-\frac{hc}{\lambda_0},\qquad \frac{eV_0}{4}=\frac{hc}{2\lambda}-\frac{hc}{\lambda_0}.\] Multiplying the second equation by \(4\) and equating to the first, \[\frac{hc}{\lambda}-\frac{hc}{\lambda_0}=\frac{2hc}{\lambda}-\frac{4hc}{\lambda_0}\ \Rightarrow\ \frac{3}{\lambda_0}=\frac{1}{\lambda}.\] Therefore \(\lambda_0=3\lambda\) and the correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.13: Filling the core gives \(\mu_r=1+\chi_m=1+2\times10^{-2}=1.02\), so \(B=\mu_rB_0=1.02B_0\). The percentage increase is \[\frac{B-B_0}{B_0}\times100=0.02\times100=2\%.\] Hence the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.14: Current sensitivity \(S_I=\dfrac{NBA}{C}\) and voltage sensitivity \(S_V=\dfrac{NBA}{CG}=\dfrac{S_I}{G}\). Since the coil resistance \(G\) is kept constant, \(S_V\propto S_I\), so a \(25\%\) increase in current sensitivity produces a \(25\%\) increase in voltage sensitivity. Hence the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.15: For simple harmonic motion \[KE=\tfrac12m\omega^2\left(A^2-x^2\right).\] This is maximum at the mean position \(x=0\) and falls to zero at the extreme position \(x=A\), and the dependence on \(x\) is a downward-opening parabola. The option graph starting at a maximum on the \(KE\) axis and curving down to zero at \(x=A\) is the fourth image, so the correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.16: A linear scale satisfies \[\frac{X-X_{freeze}}{X_{boil}-X_{freeze}}=\frac{F-32}{212-32}.\] With \(X=-95^{\circ}X\), \(X_{freeze}=-15\), \(X_{boil}=65\), \[\frac{-95-(-15)}{65-(-15)}=\frac{-80}{80}=-1=\frac{F-32}{180}.\] So \(F-32=-180\) and \(F=-148^{\circ}F\). authoredSolutions.17: Statement I is correct: the astronomical unit, parsec and light year are all units of astronomical distance. authoredSolutions.18: At the same temperature \[v_{rms}=\sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}}\propto \frac{1}{\sqrt M}.\] The molar masses increase in the order neon \((20)\), chlorine \((71)\), uranium hexafluoride \((352)\), so the root mean square speeds decrease in that order: \(v_{rms}(\text{mono})>v_{rms}(\text{dia})>v_{rms}(\text{poly})\). authoredSolutions.19: The average force equals the rate of momentum carried away by the bullets, \(F=n\,m\,v\), where \(n\) is the number fired per second. Therefore \[n=\frac{F}{mv}=\frac{125}{\left(10\times10^{-3}\right)(250)}=\frac{125}{2.5}=50.\] Hence the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.20: The half life of \(A\) is \(T_{1/2}=\dfrac{\ln 2}{\lambda_A}\) and the average (mean) life of \(B\) is \(\tau=\dfrac{1}{\lambda_B}\). Equating them, \[\frac{\ln 2}{\lambda_A}=\frac{1}{\lambda_B}\ \Rightarrow\ \lambda_A=\lambda_B\ln 2.\] Hence the correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.21: Six different wavelengths require \(\dfrac{n(n-1)}{2}=6\), i.e. \(n=4\), so the atom is excited from \(n=1\) to \(n=4\). authoredSolutions.22: By the lens maker's formula, for a biconvex lens with \(R_1=+R\) and \(R_2=-R\), \[P=\left(\mu_{rel}-1\right)\left(\frac{2}{R}\right).\] In air \(\mu_{rel}=1.8\), in the liquid \(\mu_{rel}=\dfrac{1.8}{1.5}=1.2\). authoredSolutions.24: For a force varying with position, \[W=\int_0^4(2+3x)\,dx=\left[2x+\frac{3x^2}{2}\right]_0^4=8+24=32\text{ J}.\] Hence the answer is \(32\).
authoredSolutions.25: From the figure the incline makes \(30^{\circ}\) with the horizontal, one charge sits at height \(h\) and the other at the foot of the incline, so their separation along the incline is \(r=\dfrac{h}{\sin 30^{\circ}}=2h\). authoredSolutions.26: For a solid sphere, the moment of inertia about a diameter is \(I_d=\tfrac{2}{5}mR^2\) and, by the parallel axis theorem, about a tangent it is \[I_t=\tfrac{2}{5}mR^2+mR^2=\tfrac{7}{5}mR^2.\] The angular momentum about the diameter is \(L=I_d\omega=\tfrac{2}{5}mR^2\omega\). authoredSolutions.27: Within the elastic limit the tension is proportional to the extension, \(T=k\left(l-l_0\right)\), so \[\frac{100}{120}=\frac{l_1-l_0}{l_2-l_0}\ \Rightarrow\ 5l_2-5l_0=6l_1-6l_0\ \Rightarrow\ l_0=6l_1-5l_2.\] Using \(10l_2=11l_1\), i.e. \(l_2=\dfrac{11l_1}{10}\), \[l_0=6l_1-5\times\frac{11l_1}{10}=6l_1-\frac{11l_1}{2}=\frac{l_1}{2}.\] Hence \(x=2\).
authoredSolutions.28: From the graph the field rises linearly, passing through \(B=10\text{ mT}\) at \(t=5\text{ s}\), so \(B=2t\text{ mT}\) and \(\dfrac{dB}{dt}=2\text{ mT s}^{-1}\) (constant between \(t=2\text{ s}\) and \(t=4\text{ s}\)). authoredSolutions.29: A projectile is at the same height at two instants symmetric about the top of the trajectory, so the total time of flight is \(T=t_1+t_2=3+5=8\text{ s}\). authoredSolutions.30: In the figure the two cells are connected with their positive terminals facing each other, so they oppose: the net emf is \(8-4=4\text{ V}\). authoredSolutions.91: The terminal velocity of a small sphere in a viscous medium is \(v\propto r^2\). Volume conservation for eight drops coalescing gives \[8\times\tfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3=\tfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3\ \Rightarrow\ R=2r.\] Hence \[\frac{v_{new}}{v_{old}}=\left(\frac{R}{r}\right)^2=4\ \Rightarrow\ v_{new}=4\times10=40\text{ cm/s}.\] The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.92: Car \(Q\) (the observer) chases car \(P\) (the source), so the observer moves towards the source and the source moves away from the observer: \[f'=f_0\left(\frac{v+v_o}{v+v_s}\right)=400\left(\frac{360+40}{360+20}\right)=400\times\frac{400}{380}\approx 421\text{ Hz}.\] Hence the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.93: For a plane electromagnetic wave, \[\left|\vec B\right|=\frac{\left|\vec E\right|}{c}=\frac{6.6}{3\times10^{8}}=2.2\times10^{-8}\text{ T}.\] The direction follows from \(\hat E\times\hat B=\hat c\). With \(\hat E=\hat j\) and \(\hat c=\hat i\), we need \(\hat j\times\hat B=\hat i\), and since \(\hat j\times\hat k=\hat i\), \(\hat B=\hat k\). Therefore \(\vec B=2.2\times10^{-8}\hat k\text{ T}\) and the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.94: By Gauss's law the flux through any closed surface depends only on the enclosed charge. The surface encloses the positive plate, which carries charge \(Q=CV\), so \[\phi=\frac{q_{enc}}{\varepsilon_0}=\frac{CV}{\varepsilon_0}.\] Hence the correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.95: Write \(\left[\rho\right]=\left[F\right]^a\left[V\right]^b\left[T\right]^c\), i.e. \[ML^{-3}=\left(MLT^{-2}\right)^a\left(LT^{-1}\right)^b T^{c}=M^{a}L^{a+b}T^{-2a-b+c}.\] Comparing powers: \(a=1\); \(a+b=-3\Rightarrow b=-4\); \(-2a-b+c=0\Rightarrow -2+4+c=0\Rightarrow c=-2\). Therefore \[\left[\rho\right]=FV^{-4}T^{-2},\] and the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.96: In satellite communication the C-band is used, with the uplink (earth station to satellite) at the higher frequency and the downlink (satellite to earth station) at the lower one. The standard C-band uplink is \(5.925-6.425\text{ GHz}\), while \(3.7-4.2\text{ GHz}\) is the corresponding downlink; \(76-88\text{ MHz}\) and \(420-890\text{ MHz}\) are terrestrial broadcast bands. Hence the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.97: Inside a uniform sphere the gravitational potential at distance \(r\) from the centre is \[V(r)=-\frac{GM}{2R^3}\left(3R^2-r^2\right).\] At the surface \(\left(r=R\right)\), \(V=-\dfrac{GM}{R}\); at the centre \(\left(r=0\right)\), \(V_0=-\dfrac{3GM}{2R}\). Therefore \[V_0=\frac{3}{2}V.\] Hence the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.98: From \(v=10\sqrt x\) we get \(v^2=100x\). Differentiating with respect to \(x\), \[2v\frac{dv}{dx}=100\ \Rightarrow\ a=v\frac{dv}{dx}=50\text{ m s}^{-2}.\] Then \[F=ma=0.5\times 50=25\text{ N}.\] Hence the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.99: The vertical component is \(u_y=40\sin 30^{\circ}=20\text{ m s}^{-1}\), so at \(t=2\text{ s}\), \[v_y=20-10(2)=0,\] i.e. the projectile is at the top of its path. authoredSolutions.100: For reflection at a plane mirror the deviation of the ray is \[\delta=180^{\circ}-2i,\] where \(i\) is the angle of incidence, equal to the angle of reflection. With \(i=30^{\circ}\), \[\delta=180^{\circ}-60^{\circ}=120^{\circ}.\] Hence the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.101: For an orbit close to the surface, \(v_o=\sqrt{gR}\) and the escape speed is \(v_e=\sqrt{2gR}\). Here \[v_o=\sqrt{10\times 6.4\times10^{6}}=8\times10^{3}\text{ m/s}=8\text{ km/s}.\] The extra speed required is \[\Delta v=v_e-v_o=\left(\sqrt2-1\right)\sqrt{gR}=8\left(\sqrt2-1\right)\text{ km/s}.\] Hence the correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.102: For the same kinetic energy \(K\), \(p=\sqrt{2mK}\), so \[\lambda=\frac{h}{p}\propto\frac{1}{\sqrt m}\ \Rightarrow\ \frac{\lambda_p}{\lambda_e}=\sqrt{\frac{m_e}{m_p}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1849}}=\frac{1}{43}.\] Hence the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.103: For an ideal gas the internal energy depends only on temperature, \(U=nC_VT\). The process in which the temperature is constant is the isothermal process, so the internal energy stays constant. Hence the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.104: For a hydrogen-like ion, \[E_n=-13.6\frac{Z^2}{n^2}\text{ eV}.\] For the singly ionised helium ion \(Z=2\), and the first excited state is \(n=2\), so \[E_2=-13.6\times\frac{4}{4}=-13.6\text{ eV}.\] Hence the correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.105: From the figure the inputs \(A\) and \(B\) feed an OR gate and an AND gate; their outputs feed a NAND gate whose output passes through an inverter. authoredSolutions.106: With \(T=27^{\circ}C=300\text{ K}\), \[v_{rms}=\sqrt{\frac{3k_BT}{m}}=\sqrt{\frac{3\times1.4\times10^{-23}\times300}{4.6\times10^{-26}}}=\sqrt{2.74\times10^{5}}\approx523\text{ m/s}.\] Hence the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.107: From the figure the battery of \(8\text{ V}\) is connected between \(E\) and \(A\), and \(R_6\) sits directly across it, so it does not affect the branch through \(R_5\). authoredSolutions.108: We are told \(\vec B-\vec A=2\hat j\), so \[\vec B=\vec A+2\hat j=2\hat i+5\hat j+2\hat k.\] Therefore \[\left|\vec B\right|=\sqrt{2^2+5^2+2^2}=\sqrt{33}.\] Hence the correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.109: As the magnet falls through the metallic pipe the flux through the pipe wall changes, inducing eddy currents. By Lenz's law these oppose the relative motion, producing a retarding force, so the magnet takes longer to fall than an identical non-magnetic bar. Both statements are true and the reason correctly explains the assertion, so the correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.110: Inside a long solenoid the magnetic field is along the axis, and the electron moves along the same axis, so \(\vec v\parallel\vec B\) and \[\vec F=q\left(\vec v\times\vec B\right)=0.\] With no force the electron is neither deflected nor accelerated and continues to move along the axis, so statements B and C alone are correct. Hence the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.111: From the figure, \(C_3\), \(C_4\) and \(C_5\) form a series path between the two middle nodes: \[\frac{1}{C_{345}}=\frac12+\frac14+\frac12=\frac54\ \Rightarrow\ C_{345}=0.8\ \mu F.\] This is in parallel with \(C_2=0.2\ \mu F\), giving \(1.0\ \mu F\), which is in series with \(C_1=2\ \mu F\) and \(C_6=2\ \mu F\): \[\frac{1}{C_{eq}}=\frac12+1+\frac12=2\ \Rightarrow\ C_{eq}=0.5\ \mu F.\] The charge drawn from the source is \(Q=0.5\times10=5\ \mu C\).
